reviews.reasoning: Numbering re-derived first: Ps 32 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json; psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions['32'] = {mt_title_verses: prefix_of_v1, labels: [maskil, le_david]}), so every web:Ps.32.V = oshb:Ps.32.V and the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.32.0 binds to oshb:Ps.32.1, whose bytes open לְדָוִ֗ד מַ֫שְׂכִּ֥יל before the beatitude. The row's dual-cites are therefore arithmetically sound and its maskil/le_david labels match the inventory exactly. All three Hebrew runs the row quotes collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs (אַשְׁרֵ֥י at oshb:Ps.32.1; אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי אָדָ֗ם at oshb:Ps.32.2; כִּֽי הֶ֭חֱרַשְׁתִּי at oshb:Ps.32.3), and each gloss covers the same span as its quote. The selah disclosure is complete and correct against pmarks_Ps.json: Ps 32 holds exactly 3 selah verses (MT Ps.32.4, Ps.32.5, Ps.32.7), all 3 inside this span, all 3 disclosed, and the row correctly demotes them to corroboration of a seam driven by the speaker change at web:Ps.32.8 — selah does not carry the seam here. Confidence high is earned by that driver. One defect: the device_notes close with a seg-layer absence claim that the disclosure inventory contradicts.

challenges.claim: The device_notes claim that no further Ps 32 marks-layer device is attested is false: pmarks_Ps.json records five paseq segs in Psalm 32, three of them inside this row's own span.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json paseq (seg layer, single-witness, MT-keyed) records Psalm 32 at MT Ps.32.4, Ps.32.6, Ps.32.7, Ps.32.8 and Ps.32.9 — 5 verses of the psalm's 11 carry a paseq seg, 5 segs in 5 verses (book-wide inventory: 481 verses, 522 segs). Ps 32 is an identity psalm, so web:Ps.32.4 = oshb:Ps.32.4, web:Ps.32.6 = oshb:Ps.32.6 and web:Ps.32.7 = oshb:Ps.32.7 all fall inside the span Ps.32.1-Ps.32.7, and the seam verse pair web:Ps.32.7 = oshb:Ps.32.7 | web:Ps.32.8 = oshb:Ps.32.8 carries one on each side. The acrostic half of the same sentence is sound — psalm_device_inventory.json keys its acrostics table at 9, 10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, 119 and 145 (9 psalms), with no entry for 32 — and the selah half is exact (3 verses: MT Ps.32.4, Ps.32.5, Ps.32.7). Only the blanket 'no further ... device is attested' clause is wrong; the repair is to disclose the paseq count with its '(single-witness)' tag rather than to assert absence.

reviews.reasoning: Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs: אַשְׂכִּֽילְךָ֨ וְֽאוֹרְךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.32.8 and וְהַבּוֹטֵ֥חַ בַּיהוָ֑ה at oshb:Ps.32.10. The first is the quotation-discipline test of this span and the row passes it: WLC carries a paseq seg between those two words (pmarks_Ps.json paseq at MT Ps.32.8, single-witness), and the row quotes the staged verse bytes without importing the seg character into the quoted run — correct, since paseq is not quotable verse text. Numbering is identity throughout Ps 32, so every dual-cite in the row resolves 1:1. Glosses cover their quoted spans exactly, and the four WEB renderings the argument leans on are verbatim at their inline refs. The selah handling is right in both directions: the front-seam selah at MT Ps.32.7 is disclosed, the span's own four verses carry none (pmarks_Ps.json lists only Ps.32.4, Ps.32.5, Ps.32.7 for this psalm), and device_notes states explicitly that selah corroborates rather than drives. The driver is the speaker change at web:Ps.32.8 = oshb:Ps.32.8, and the row flags it as a reading ('read here as') rather than asserting the identification — the honest treatment of a genuinely contested voice, and medium confidence is calibrated to it rather than to the seam's obviousness. No count, form, quote, or arithmetic defect found.

The row's inventory-facing claims are all re-derived and correct: psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions['33'] is null (Ps 33 carries no title, so there is no Ps.33.0 pseudo-ref to cite), hodu_openings lists Ps.33.2 among its 6 entries (MT Ps.33.2, Ps.105.1, Ps.107.1, Ps.118.1, Ps.118.29, Ps.136.1), the acrostics table is keyed exactly at 9, 10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, 119, 145 as quoted, and Ps 33 does run to 22 verses in both witnesses — so the row's 'no acrostic is claimed' disclosure is the right handling of a 22-verse psalm that is not an acrostic. Ps 33 is an identity psalm, so its dual-cites resolve 1:1. All five Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier, and each gloss covers its quote's span. The seam driver is sound: the imperative address stops after web:Ps.33.3 and כִּֽי (oshb:Ps.33.4) opens a motive clause, which is a tier-1 discourse shift and warrants the high confidence. Two defects sit in the supporting claims rather than in the seam: the rejected_alternative's terminus is contradicted by the bytes at web:Ps.33.20-22, and the imperative count does not name the object it counts.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's clause 'no further congregational imperative until web:Ps.33.20-22' is false — those three verses contain no imperative at all and do not address the congregation — so it posits an imperative frame for the psalm that neither witness carries.
challenges.evidence: Ps 33 is identity (web_mt_offset_map.json), so web:Ps.33.20-22 = oshb:Ps.33.20-22. Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collated at byte tier, the finite forms in those three verses are חִכְּתָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.33.20), יִשְׂמַ֣ח and בָטָֽחְנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.21), יְהִֽי and יִחַ֥לְנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.22) — 5 finite verbs across 3 verses, comprising a singular suffix-conjugation, a prefix-conjugation, two 1cp suffix-conjugations and a short-form jussive. Not one is an imperative. The addressee across the three verses is Yahweh, not the congregation: חַסְדְּךָ֣ and לָֽךְ (oshb:Ps.33.22) carry 2ms reference, whereas the imperatives of web:Ps.33.1-3 address צַ֭דִּיקִים (oshb:Ps.33.1). WEB agrees at every point: “Our soul has waited for” (web:Ps.33.20), “For our heart rejoices in” (web:Ps.33.21), “Let your loving kindness be on” (web:Ps.33.22) — a declarative pair plus a jussive petition. The staged extract carries no morphology codes, so this is argued from the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings. The seam warrant survives intact without the clause; the terminus should be deleted, not re-anchored, since no congregational imperative returns anywhere after web:Ps.33.3.

challenges.claim: The count 'three consecutive plural imperatives' names no swept object and carries no digit-bearing sweep; the span actually holds five plural imperative forms, and only the verse-initial subset numbers three.
challenges.evidence: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and byte-collated, Ps 33:1-3 carries 5 plural imperative forms across 3 verses, not 3: רַנְּנ֣וּ (oshb:Ps.33.1); הוֹד֣וּ and זַמְּרוּ (oshb:Ps.33.2); שִֽׁירוּ and הֵיטִ֥יבוּ (oshb:Ps.33.3). WEB renders all five as imperatives: “Rejoice in Yahweh, you” (web:Ps.33.1), “Give thanks to Yahweh with the lyre. Sing praises to” (web:Ps.33.2), “Sing to him a new song. Play” (web:Ps.33.3). The three the row names are exactly the VERSE-INITIAL imperatives (3 of 3 verses), which is a real and load-bearing pattern — naming that object before the numeral ('three verse-initial plural imperatives, one per verse') would make the count exact without touching the warrant.

reviews.reasoning: All three quoted runs collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs (כִּֽי יָשָׁ֥ר דְּבַר יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Ps.33.4; בִּדְבַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה שָׁמַ֣יִם נַעֲשׂ֑וּ at oshb:Ps.33.6; עֲצַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תַּעֲמֹ֑ד at oshb:Ps.33.11), and every gloss covers precisely its quoted span — including the tight כִּֽי citation in observed_substrate_signals. Identity numbering makes all four dual-cites exact. The span arithmetic checks: Ps.33.4-Ps.33.11 is 8 verses, matching the row's 'eight-verse span' and sitting at the top of the ~4-8 verse strophe policy. The device absence claim is span-scoped and true: pmarks_Ps.json lists no selah anywhere in Ps 33 and no paseq inside 33:4-11 (the psalm's single paseq seg is at MT Ps.33.12, outside this span), and the acrostics table has no Ps 33 entry — so 'no selah or acrostic marker' overclaims nothing. The rejected alternative engages the real rival (a 33:4-9 | 33:10-11 split) and answers it on discourse grounds rather than taste. I tested one further rival the row does not name: the jussive יִֽירְא֣וּ (oshb:Ps.33.8), “Let all the earth fear” (web:Ps.33.8), does widen the addressee mid-span — but it is four verses from the front seam and three from the back, so it is not a seam-adjacent rival and does not disturb either edge. Medium confidence is honest for a unit whose internal cohesion is topical.

The front seam is well chosen and I support the span: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הַ֭גּוֹי (oshb:Ps.33.12) collates at BYTE tier and is a tier-1 formulaic opener, and the psalm's one paseq seg (pmarks_Ps.json, MT Ps.33.12, single-witness) happens to sit in that same verse without being claimed as evidence — correct restraint, since a seg-layer mark could not drive the seam anyway. Identity numbering makes both cross-psalm dual-cites to Ps 32 exact, and those two verses are properly mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs as out-of-span argued verses. The back seam at web:Ps.33.19|web:Ps.33.20 is corroborated from the far side by the person shift, and medium confidence is defensible. Two defects, both in evidence hygiene rather than in the seam: the 33:18 gloss reaches past its quoted run, and the Ps 32 beatitude is counted as one use when the bytes carry two. I also note without filing it that device_notes locates Ps 32 as 'the preceding psalm of this part', where 'this part' reads as the campaign partition rather than anything verse-anchored; the phrase 'reuses, in its own wording' is similarly self-referential. Both are register observations, and I leave them as observations because the referent is ambiguous enough that I will not rest a challenge on it.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync at oshb:Ps.33.18: the English gloss renders two source tokens that the Hebrew quote stops short of.
challenges.evidence: The quoted run הִנֵּ֤ה עֵ֣ין יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Ps.33.18) collates at byte tier and ends at the divine name. The gloss attached to it, “Behold, Yahweh’s eye is on those who fear him” (web:Ps.33.18), renders two further tokens of the same verse — אֶל יְרֵאָ֑יו (oshb:Ps.33.18) — which the quoted run does not contain. Quote spans and their glosses must cover the same span, and the repair must re-cut rather than truncate: either extend the quote to הִנֵּ֤ה עֵ֣ין יְ֭הוָה אֶל יְרֵאָ֑יו or cut the gloss back to “Behold, Yahweh’s eye” (web:Ps.33.18). The same desync recurs at oshb:Ps.33.22 in the span Ps.33.20-Ps.33.22, so the cure is a single authored pattern applied to both.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative counts the Ps 32 beatitude as used 'once already' while citing web:Ps.32.1-2, but the particle stands in two verses there.
challenges.evidence: Ps 32 is identity, so web:Ps.32.1 = oshb:Ps.32.1 and web:Ps.32.2 = oshb:Ps.32.2. Both verses carry the beatitude particle and both forms collate at byte tier: אַשְׁרֵ֥י (oshb:Ps.32.1) and אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי (oshb:Ps.32.2), whose pointing differs by a meteg — 2 verses, 2 occurrences. WEB renders both: “Blessed is he whose disobedience is” (web:Ps.32.1), “Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh doesn’t” (web:Ps.32.2). The row covering Ps.32.1-Ps.32.7 calls the same pair a paired beatitude, so the two rows disagree about the same bytes. Note the sweep hazard behind the correct figure: a book-wide skeleton sweep of the consonantal string returns 31 verses, but the skeleton conflates the beatitude particle with the 'steps' noun (oshb:Ps.17.5, oshb:Ps.73.2 among them), so the pointed byte check per verse — not the skeleton count — is what settles Ps 32 at 2 verses.

reviews.reasoning: The seam is right and the span holds: the 1cp suffixes נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ, עֶזְרֵ֖נוּ and וּמָגִנֵּ֣נוּ (oshb:Ps.33.20) open a congregational voice that is absent from web:Ps.33.13-19, and it runs unbroken to the psalm's end through בָטָֽחְנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.21) and יִחַ֥לְנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.22) — a genuine tier-1 person shift, not a topical one, so high confidence is earned even for a 3-verse row. Both quoted runs collate at BYTE tier, identity numbering makes the dual-cites exact, and the out-of-span verses argued in prose are all mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs. The device absence statement is span-scoped and true (pmarks_Ps.json has no selah, no paseq and no acrostic entry for these three verses; the psalm's one paseq seg is at MT Ps.33.12). The defects are in how the substrate is described, not in what it shows: the row twice calls its lead form a verb when it is a noun, and the closing gloss overruns its quote.

challenges.claim: The lead substrate signal misdescribes its form: it calls נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.20) a 'plural self-reference verb', but the token is a noun carrying a 1cp suffix and the clause's finite verb is a singular suffix-conjugation.
challenges.evidence: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and byte-collated, oshb:Ps.33.20 opens נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ חִכְּתָ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֑ה. נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ is the noun with a 1cp pronominal suffix — the row's own gloss and WEB agree, both rendering it as the clause's subject: “Our soul has waited for” (web:Ps.33.20). The finite verb is חִכְּתָ֣ה, a singular suffix-conjugation form agreeing with that singular subject; nothing in the verse is a plural-inflected verb. The psalm's first 1cp-inflected VERBS arrive later, at בָטָֽחְנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.21) and יִחַ֥לְנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.22) — 2 such verbs in the span. The error is repeated verbatim in the rationale and in observed_substrate_signals, so the seam-pair cure is one edit installed in both fields. The underlying signal is real and easily rescued: the 1cp reference enters at נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ, עֶזְרֵ֖נוּ and וּמָגִנֵּ֣נוּ (oshb:Ps.33.20) as suffixed nouns, and the row should say so rather than assign a verb class. The staged extract carries no morphology codes, so this is argued from the pointed bytes and both witnesses.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync at oshb:Ps.33.22: the closing gloss renders a token outside the quoted run.
challenges.evidence: The quoted run יְהִֽי חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.33.22) collates at byte tier and stops at the divine name. Its gloss, “Let your loving kindness be on” (web:Ps.33.22), renders עָלֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Ps.33.22), which the quoted run does not contain. Re-cut the gloss to “Let your loving kindness” (web:Ps.33.22) or extend the quote to יְהִֽי חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ — extension without a matching re-cut, or truncation of the Hebrew to dodge the parity check, would both be regressions. The identical pattern appears at oshb:Ps.33.18 in the span Ps.33.12-Ps.33.19; one authored cure covers both.
